$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-4,-1,5)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $-4x-2y+2z=16.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-1$ and $y=2$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-4x-2y+2z & =16 \\ -4(-1)-2(2)+2z & =16 \\ 2z & =16 \\ z & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-1,2,8)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-1,2,8⟩-⟨-4,-1,5⟩ \\  & =⟨3,3,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨-4,-2,2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|3\cdot (-4)+3\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-12-6+6|}{\sqrt{16+4+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,-12\,|}{\sqrt{24}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-1,0,2)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $2x-y+2z=-1.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=2$ and $y=3$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y+2z & =-1 \\ 2(2)-(3)+2z & =-1 \\ 2z & =-2 \\ z & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(2,3,-1)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,3,-1⟩-⟨-1,0,2⟩ \\  & =⟨3,3,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨2,-1,2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|3\cdot 2+3\cdot (-1)+(-3)\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|6-3-6|}{\sqrt{4+1+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,-3\,|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Given that $Q(1,-2,-1)$ lies on the plane $\Pi:\mathbf{r} \cdot \langle 2, 0, -2 \rangle = 4,$ find the shortest distance from $P(0 , -1 , 2)$ to $\Pi.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,-2,-1⟩-⟨0,-1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $\mathbf{n}= \langle 2, 0, -2 \rangle.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2+0+6|}{\sqrt{4+0+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,8\,|}{\sqrt{8}} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

                    Finding the Shortest Distance Between a Point and a Plane Given in Cartesian Form
canonical_examples.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(3 , -10 , 3)$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equation $2x+y-2z = -1$.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=4$ and $y=-5$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+y-2z & =-1 \\ 2(4)+(-5)+1 & =2z \\ 4 & =2z \\ z & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(4, -5, 2)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overrightarrow{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨4,-5,2⟩-⟨3,-10,3⟩ \\  & =⟨1,5,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $\mathbf{n}=\langle a,b,c \rangle.$ So, for the plane $\Pi,$ we have $\mathbf{n}= \langle 2, 1, -2 \rangle.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot 2+5\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2+5+2|}{\sqrt{4+1+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,9\,|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.problem:
Suppose we want to find the shortest distance between the point $P(3,0,-2)$ and the plane $\Pi$ that is given by the equation 

$$
(\mathbf{r}-\langle 2 , 3 , 1 \rangle ) \cdot \langle 4 , 4 , 2 \rangle = 0.
$$

 

First, note that $\mathbf{n} = \langle 4 , 4 , 2 \rangle$ is a vector that's normal to the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14147962/assets/7b2dfcd87c1f5e4e2c2b1a0b9a7f73899772e33e1020465b2b38d1b2de29a66c.png)

Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(2,3,1)$. Then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,3,1⟩-⟨3,0,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,3,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The shortest distance $d$ from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14147962/assets/26e494eef47db4dba3ac36dfa96c7e9a9d191321b22bb82874f3e74bbd7116ef.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot 4+3\cdot 4+3\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-4+12+6|}{\sqrt{16+16+4}} \\  & =\frac{|14|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{7}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is $\dfrac{7}{3}.$
